transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-29
Start time (UTC): 16:00
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Oscar (Redwood SE), Ravi (Redwood SE), Liam (CTO Quantix), Priya (Platform), Jorge (SecOps), Ana (ML)
body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro, I'm Maya, AE at Redwood. Oscar and Ravi are our SEs. How are you all?
[00:08] Liam O'Connor: Good, thanks. Busy week but excited to dig in.
[00:11] Oscar Ruiz: Great. Goal for today is to understand your integration constraints — SDK vs gateway/sidecar, LangChain/LlamaIndex usage, and security needs (VPC/HSM). We'll also surface tradeoffs between Hosted, Dedicated and Private.
[00:25] Priya Nair: Our immediate aim is to replace an in-house proxy that fans calls to OpenAI and an internal LLM cluster. We're evaluating Redwood because of the batching/kv cache claims and want to know how to fit the SDK into our stack. We use LangChain in some services, LlamaIndex in others.
[00:40] Oscar Ruiz: Helpful — do you call the models directly from backend services or via a gateway today?
[00:45] Ana Torres: Mostly backend services call a central gateway (nginx + custom auth) that handles rate limiting and routing. We also have some serverless Lambdas that call directly.
[00:54] Ravi Patel: When you say rate limiting, is that per-user, per-API-key, or per-route?
[00:58] Priya Nair: Per-customer initially, per-route for heavy endpoints. We also need token quotas for users in tiered plans.
[01:05] Jorge Silva: From security: we need SOC2 readiness, audit logs for all token-level requests, SSO/SAML, RBAC. Also interested in KMS integration or HSM for keys if we go private.
[01:16] Oscar Ruiz: That aligns with Redwood offerings. Hosted provides quick onboarding but logs live in Redwood. Dedicated gives you reserved capacity, per-customer isolation, and Private adds the private control plane + VPC/on-prem for KMS. For keys, we support customer-managed KMS and HSM via integrations when you're on Private.
[01:35] Liam O'Connor: Performance wise, our concern is tail latency for chat experiences — we need <200ms token latency for short prompts or close to that. How does that map to Hosted vs Dedicated?
[01:47] Oscar Ruiz: Tail latency depends on placement and batching. Dedicated is easiest to guarantee latency because we size GPU pools and reduce noisy neighbors. Hosted can be tuned with model pinning and priority routing but may have occasional variability. We can run a benchmark to quantify — that'll be part of the SE deep dive.
[02:03] Priya Nair: On the integration pattern: is Redwood SDK blocking only, or do you support streaming and event-based hooks? We rely on streaming in chat.
[02:11] Ravi Patel: SDK supports sync and streaming, same as the HTTP API. We also have a lightweight sidecar that teams can run which implements connection pooling, auto-retries, and local prefix caching if you want to keep routing control in-house. The gateway route pattern is also common — front your requests through a central gateway that talks to Redwood. Sidecar reduces egress and gives per-instance batching control.
[02:35] Ana Torres: Hmm, sidecar vs gateway — what are the observability differences? We need traces tied to user IDs and cost breakdown per token per request.
[02:44] Oscar Ruiz: We emit request-level metrics and token-level cost estimates via our observability hooks. You can attach trace_id and user_id in headers; those propagate into our Console. We also provide per-route dashboards and cost breakdowns—plus traces that correlate to your tracing system (we have OpenTelemetry exporters).
[03:03] Jorge Silva: Are those hooks available in Private? We can't have data plane telemetry leaving our VPC except aggregated metrics.
[03:11] Oscar Ruiz: In Private you keep the data plane and control the telemetry export. You can configure an OTLP endpoint in your network and we push metrics there, or we can run an agent that exports only aggregated metrics to Redwood Console if you choose. Logs for audit must stay in your storage if required.
[03:26] Liam O'Connor: LangChain/LlamaIndex — any recommended patterns? Our ML team uses LangChain wrappers and LlamaIndex connectors. We need embedding pipelines too.
[03:36] Ravi Patel: Common pattern: use Redwood SDK as the backing provider in LangChain and LlamaIndex. We have sample connectors for both. For embeddings, we recommend batched embedding endpoints and caching embeddings in your DB. For retrieval augmented generation (RAG) we recommend prefix caching + KV cache on the runtime for repeated queries to reduce token cost.
[03:56] Priya Nair: Example: if we run similarity search for a customer support RAG, how do you recommend rate limits to avoid runaway cost?
[04:02] Oscar Ruiz: Two layers: client-side quotas (in your gateway) for request frequency and Redwood-enforced per-key quotas. Redwood supports per-route and per-api-key rate limiting and token quotas with alerts. Also quota resets and soft-limits for pilot phases.
[04:17] Ana Torres: For streaming chat, do we get per-token accounting in real-time? We want to stop streaming if costs spike.
[04:23] Ravi Patel: Streaming includes token counts and progressive cost estimates. You can subscribe to a websocket hook or check a server-side callback to cut generation. There's also a server-side policy engine to enforce cost or length caps.
[04:36] Liam O'Connor: Network architecture question — if we go Private, do we need to open holes inbound? We prefer to initiate outbound only from our VPC to Redwood.
[04:44] Oscar Ruiz: Private supports both. For air-gapped or on-prem, our private control plane can be customer-hosted. For VPC deployments we typically peer or use private links; you can keep outbound-only by configuring an outbound proxy that pulls models from a local runtime. We'll share the network checklist.
[05:00] Priya Nair: Something practical — do you have a recommended throughput for initial pilot? We expect ~120 RPS peak across services, avg seq len 80 tokens, burst to 350 RPS during events.
[05:11] Oscar Ruiz: For those numbers we'd probably recommend starting with a small dedicated pool (1-2 GPUs depending on model size) or hosted with a dedicated concurrency reservation. SE deep dive will size it precisely. We'll run a scaled benchmark with your sample prompts; please share the traffic CSV.
[05:25] Jorge Silva: Compliance — can we retain full request logs for 90 days and have them searchable?
[05:31] Ravi Patel: Yes, with Dedicated or Private we can ship logs to your S3 and maintain retention. Hosted can do longer retention as an add-on but for strict controls Private is standard.
[05:40] Liam O'Connor: Ok, pricing — how do you bill for hosted vs dedicated? High level please.
[05:45] Maya Chen: Hosted is usage-based (per-token generation and embedding). Dedicated is reserved capacity + usage; you'll have a monthly commit with lower per-token cost and priority. Private is a licensing + support model usually with an infra fee. We'll send an example TCO sheet.
[05:58] Priya Nair: One last technical: our stack uses an internal gateway with Lua filters that attach user context. Can we still attach those headers through your SDK?
[06:05] Oscar Ruiz: Absolutely — headers like x-user-id, x-org-id, x-trace-id are supported and map into Console. If the gateway is doing TLS termination, ensure mTLS between gateway and Redwood in Private for mutual auth.
[06:17] Ana Torres: Any gotchas with LlamaIndex? We had an issue where streaming outputs are chunked and LlamaIndex concatenation caused prompt drift.
[06:25] Ravi Patel: We see that — recommended fix is to use Redwood streaming with delimiter tokens and a small reassembly layer. Also keep a consistent tokenizer/version across embedding and generation models. We'll share a LlamaIndex troubleshooting note.
[06:40] Liam O'Connor: What about fallbacks — if a model is overloaded or we lose capacity can Redwood automatically fallback to a smaller quantized model?
[06:48] Oscar Ruiz: Yes — routing policies can fallback to compatible variants (quantized or smaller arch) based on latency/cost rules. You can set those policies per-route. We also support automatic canary rollouts and A/B.
[06:58] Priya Nair: For pilot, we want: 1) integration sample with LangChain, 2) a small dedicated bench to see latencies, 3) security review.
[07:06] Maya Chen: That's a good summary. We'll deliver the LangChain/LlamaIndex repo, propose benchmark dates, and send the Private deployment checklist.
[07:14] Liam O'Connor: Great. Anything else from Redwood?
[07:17] Oscar Ruiz: We'll also put together a side-by-side doc: gateway vs sidecar vs direct SDK with perf and observability differences.
[07:24] Jorge Silva: And please include audit log retention options and KMS/HSM specifics.
[07:29] Maya Chen: Noted — we'll include that.
[07:32] End summary and next steps: runbook + bench scheduling + security artifacts.

Notes: There were a few transcription artifacts and overlaps, e.g., names occasionally mis-tagged by the recorder.
